text:
maya: quick sketch of a measurement protocol for onboarding speculative decoding onto a new quantized build — throwing it here for feedback before i turn it into a runbook

jon: SGTM, paste the commands + artifact locations too. main flags in my head: reproducibility, cadence for seeds, and how we decide accept/reject.

maya: high-level plan: paired-run replay. spin two identical runners on same hardware: control (spec=false) vs experiment (spec=true). replay an identical request list to both in identical order, capture raw outputs + perf traces. keep RNG seeds pinned and log them. produce token-level diffs and corpus metrics.

ravi: how do you ensure identical ordering under the runtime? theres usually some inter-request shuffling in our benches.

maya: good call. we use the deterministic replay harness (replayd) that pins ordering and timestamps; it injects requests at recorded arrival times. alternative is to run single-threaded feeder to guarantee ordering. also capture request IDs to map responses.

sophie: list the metrics you want in the initial pass?

maya: compact metrics list:
- latency: p50/p90/p95 end-to-end, per-token latency, first-token vs steady-state
- throughput: tokens/sec and requests/sec at various batch sizes
- perf: GPU util, memory, kernel time breakdown, KV cache hit-rate
- quality: token-level cross-entropy delta, EM for QA, token-F1/ROUGE for summarization, embedding cosine agreement against baseline responses
- safety: hallucination heuristics + small manual review sample (stratified n=200)
- stability: variance across seeds (5 independent seeds) with bootstrap CI
- fallback/failure: frequency of speculative aborts, latency spikes correlated to fallback events

derek: add an explicit acceptance criterion: pre-declare primary metric per workload. if primary metric drops >0.5pp absolute and is statistically significant (p<0.05 via paired bootstrap), fail. also flag if hallucination rate increases by >1ppt.

maya: yep. we should apply BH correction across task families to avoid too many false positives when testing many workloads.

jon: okay. practical: how do we sweep quantization variants? we have multiple builds (fp16, int8-static, int8-dynamic, qkv-tail). we need matrixed runs.

maya: run matrix plan: for each build, run control/treatment pair. Warmup: 200 short prompts to populate KV cache, then measurement window: next 2k requests. Persist raw outputs + perf traces to s3://redwood-infer-experiments/spec-decode/{build}/{spec-config}/{run_ts}/. produce a summary JSON plus raw artifacts.

ravi: can you drop a sample curl and example orchestration yaml?

maya: curl example below (dev bench):
```
curl -s -X POST http://local-runner:8080/v1/generate \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY' \ 
  -d '{"model":"our-13b-int8","speculative":true,"speculator_beams":2,"seed":42,"input":"Summarize: ..."}'
```
And the replay harness YAML pins seed + ordering and declares warmup/measurement windows.

sophie: testing stats: what's the primary significance test?

maya: paired bootstrap per-request. resample request indices with replacement, compute metric delta per resample to get CI. for latency p95 use nonparametric tests and plot tail distributions; for categorical outcomes (EM) use paired bootstrap on the indicator per request. also report effect sizes + 95% CI.

derek: also include a simple latency waterfall and kernel-level trace for any request where speculative fallback occurred. operational cutoff: if fallback rate > 2% or p95 latency >= 2x baseline, abort the rollout and send traces to #eng-oncall.

eval-bot: automated run summary uploaded: s3://redwood-infer-experiments/spec-decode/6288889999/summary.json 
eval-bot: control: our-13b-fp16, treatment: our-13b-int8+spec(beam=2) — quick numbers:
- delta EM = -0.12% (95% CI [-0.45, +0.21]) not significant
- token-xent delta = +0.002 nats/token (CI [-0.01, +0.016])
- p95 latency delta = -18% (improvement)
- fallback rate = 0.6%

ravi: can we also log token confidence histograms so we can detect calibration drift introduced by the spec path?

maya: done. summary JSON contains calibration slope, ECE buckets, and token-confidence histograms for control vs treatment. these will be surfaced in the per-build diff dashboard.

sophie: ops: maya, please convert this sketch into a runbook PR with the YAML, the exact BH correction implementation, and dashboard panel definitions. i'll pair on the BH code and make the dashboard. we should also add a short manual-review guideline for the hallucination sample.

maya: will do. i'll tag you and derek on the PR. thanks! :pray:
